scenario.title: Gen3 equalization failure falls back to Gen2
scenario.description: On link B, equalization at 8.0 GT/s cannot pass Phase 2: the endpoint (EP1, the requester in Phase 2) asks switch port DSP1 to try transmitter presets, but none reaches the figure-of-merit target. The model retries once, gives up on 8.0 GT/s and above, and falls back to the highest rate that still works: 5.0 GT/s.
scenario.symptom: The accelerator card works, but at a fraction of the bandwidth it should have. Both ends claim 16 GT/s.
faults: equalization at Gen3 on link B cannot pass phase 2

expected.summary: Link B falls back to Gen2 x16 after two failed 8.0 GT/s equalization attempts (Phase 2); the reason is logged. Links A and C reach Gen4.

scenario.what_to_look_for: On EP1's swimlane, two teal equalization blocks at Gen3 each end with a jump to Recovery.Speed and a return to L0 at Gen1. The "eq" rows in the event log show six rejected presets per attempt (FOM well below the target of 60). After the second failure DSP1 logs "rate ceiling lowered to Gen2", then performs a plain Gen1 -> Gen2 speed change (no equalization is needed at 5.0 GT/s). In lspci view, LnkSta2 shows Phase1+ but Phase2-, and LinkEqualizationRequest+. In the model EqualizationComplete stays clear after a failure; on real hardware it may read + after an unsuccessful attempt depending on the implementation, so look at the per-phase bits and LinkEqualizationRequest first.
scenario.what_this_means: A link that settles below the rate BOTH ends support, with failed equalization phases and an equalization request flag, points at the electrical channel at that rate, not at capabilities or software. Phase 2 is the downstream direction (switch transmitter -> endpoint receiver), so that direction is the first suspect. Falling back keeps the system usable but hides the problem unless someone compares LnkSta with LnkCap.
likely_root_causes: Channel loss too high at 8 GT/s: long traces, a riser, a cable, or a connector with poor margin.
Transmitter preset/coefficient settings (or BIOS/firmware equalization overrides) that do not suit this channel.
A retimer or redriver in the path that is misconfigured or marginal.
Marginal signal integrity: crosstalk, impedance discontinuity, damaged connector, contamination.
Reference clock quality problems that only show up at higher rates.
how_to_debug: lspci -vvv on both ends: LnkSta speed 5GT/s with LnkCap 16GT/s on both (pciutils 3.8+ marks '(downgraded)' only on the endpoint side); then LnkSta2: per-phase bits and LinkEqualizationRequest+ first, since EqualizationComplete may read + after a failed attempt on some implementations.
Force a retrain at 8 GT/s on the downstream port (LnkCtl2 Target Link Speed, then Retrain Link with setpci) and watch whether it falls back again.
Check AER correctable counters (Receiver Error, Bad TLP, Bad DLLP) after forcing the higher rate.
Read the equalization presets/coefficients the ports settled on, if the vendor exposes them; compare with a known-good board.
On the bench: eye/margin measurements (scope or BERT, Lane Margining at the Receiver on 16 GT/s capable parts), and swap slot, cable or riser to isolate the channel.
mystery_hints: Both ends support 16 GT/s. What could stop the link above 5 GT/s?
Which equalization phase failed, and which direction does that phase tune?
scenario.mystery_cause: 8.0 GT/s equalization fails on one link (Phase 2: the endpoint cannot tune the switch port's transmitter).
